review_candidates.title: Technical Enablement & Demo Engineer – Enterprise SaaS
review_candidates.description: Your AI Agents Handle Production. You Architect the System and Face the Customer. We're hiring a forward-deployed enablement engineer who lives at the edge of what's possible with AI — someone who designs agent-driven systems that produce enterprise-grade onboarding, documentation, and demos, then walks into the room and delivers with authority. You'll work directly with Fortune 100 brands across community engagement and social media management products, serving as both the technical architect behind the curtain and the trusted face in front of the customer. This is not a role where you write docs by hand, build decks from templates, or iterate in a chat window. You design the machinery — prompts, context layers, agent skills, verification pipelines — and the machinery does the producing. Your job is to make that machinery smarter every week. The Work Lead enterprise onboarding programs — guide admins, moderators, and business users through structured adoption sessions that compress time-to-value. Feed every lesson back into the system so the next cohort ramps even faster. Own product demos end to end — prospect calls, customer QBRs, executive showcases alongside product leadership. You build the environments, craft the narrative, run the dry runs, and cover newly shipped features the same day they land. Keep documentation and training materials perpetually current — within days of every release, not weeks. AI agents you've configured do the drafting; you verify every screenshot, every workflow step, every claim against the live product. Engineer the AI-native backbone of everything above — this is the center of gravity. You build and iterate on the prompt chains, knowledge bases, guardrails, and autonomous verification loops that let agents take over entire categories of enablement output. Success means each deliverable type requires less of your direct involvement over time. Convert field signals into organizational leverage — package recurring customer questions into self-serve resources, distill onboarding friction into structured product feedback, and publish reusable agent configs and prompt libraries to shared repos so your teammates benefit immediately. Maintain an async operating rhythm — daily standups, work-log updates, and weekly goal reviews with recorded demos that keep distributed stakeholders aligned. What You Bring An AI-native operating style that's second nature. You think in systems, not sessions. Your instinct is to build the scaffolding — context, examples, checks — that lets agents execute autonomously, then verify and ship. 3+ years working hands-on with enterprise community engagement or social media management platforms — administering, configuring, onboarding, or driving adoption for demanding organizations. Battle-tested customer presence. You've delivered live demos, trainings, or workshops to enterprise audiences and stayed composed alongside C-level stakeholders. Clear, confident spoken English is non-negotiable. A quality bar that doesn't bend. You build automated verification into agent workflows and personally audit output before it reaches a customer. Hallucinated instructions and outdated screenshots are unacceptable. Product intuition and editorial polish. Given a goal rather than a spec, you return work that's audience-aware, visually clean, and ready to represent the brand in front of a Fortune 100 logo. Fluency across frontier AI tooling. You assign real units of work to agents, swap models based on current benchmarks, and never stop experimenting. Tool loyalty takes a back seat to results. Relentless self-direction. You chase blockers down instead of flagging them up. Ownership covers the tedious work just as fully as the high-profile moments. Extras That Set You Apart Admin-level experience operating an enterprise community or social platform instance. Background in instructional design, technical writing, or curriculum architecture. Video production skills for async walkthroughs and training modules. Prior solutions engineering, sales engineering, or forward-deployed technical roles. Hands-on experience building AI assistants or chatbots over structured knowledge bases, or contributing to shared prompt and skill libraries. Why This Matters for Your Career You'll develop a skill set that's compounding faster than almost anything else in tech: the ability to design durable, shareable AI leverage — agent workflows, prompt libraries, knowledge architectures — that lets one person deliver at the scale of a full team. The AI-native operating model here isn't aspirational; it's already running. No token ceilings, no locked toolchains. If the best path forward is a model released yesterday or an agent framework nobody on the team has tried, bring it to the table. You'll have a direct hand in defining what forward-deployed customer work looks like when AI is the starting point, not an add-on.

review_candidates.description: Location: Crawley, United Kingdom Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. With over 7,500 people in the UK, operating across defence, space, aerospace, and digital security, we help build a future we can all trust. Thales supports the security and stability of our nation by providing extraordinary technology to our customers, as well as delivering social value to the UK with our products and services. We're looking for a Product Support Engineer to join our Service Operations team, supporting the Crowsnest Mission System and associated laboratory, network and support environments. This is an excellent opportunity for a technically capable and self-motivated engineer who enjoys solving problems, supporting customers, and ensuring the availability, reliability and supportability of mission-critical systems. Location: Crawley What The Role Has To Offer As a Product Support Engineer, you'll play a key role in the through-life support of complex defence systems. You'll provide technical expertise across product support, laboratory management, network administration and customer support activities, helping to ensure systems remain operational, secure and fit for purpose. Working closely with engineering teams, programme stakeholders and customers, you'll support service delivery, implement product improvements and act as a technical authority for product-related queries. What You'll Be Doing Product & Technical Support Acting as a focal point for engineering and technical support queries relating to supported products and systems. Providing technical advice to engineering teams, programme teams, manufacturing, repair organisations and customers. Supporting product investigations, fault diagnosis, repairs and corrective actions. Identifying and implementing design and supportability improvements throughout the product lifecycle. Managing technical documentation, reports, estimates and engineering deliverables. BMN Administration Administering and maintaining Business Management Network (BMN) environments. Managing system security, software updates, patches and configuration control. Maintaining network integrity, user access controls and accreditation requirements. Supporting audits and implementing corrective actions where required. Diagnosing and resolving network and system faults. Laboratory Management Maintaining a safe, secure and effective engineering laboratory environment. Manage the crypto associated with the Crowsnest laboratory Managing lab access controls, equipment configuration and utilisation. Supporting the setup, maintenance and operation of test rigs and lab infrastructure. Managing shared resources and coordinating laboratory activities across projects. Supporting procurement, calibration, maintenance and repair of laboratory equipment. Customer & Field Support Providing product support and technical guidance to customer-facing teams. Supporting activities at customer facilities when required. Acting as an interface between engineering teams, support organisations and customers. Participating in trials, demonstrations and technical engagements when required Engineering Leadership Supporting risk, opportunity and obsolescence management activities. Contributing to support solutions, reliability and maintainability improvements. Working collaboratively across multidisciplinary engineering teams. Coaching and sharing technical knowledge with colleagues and developing engineers. About You We're looking for someone with a strong engineering background and a passion for delivering effective support solutions. You'll ideally have: Experience supporting complex electronic, networked or mission systems. Strong hardware fault-finding and diagnostic skills. Experience administering and maintaining secure networked environments. Knowledge of product support, service management and through-life support principles. Experience working within engineering laboratories or test environments. An understanding of configuration, asset and equipment management. Strong stakeholder engagement and communication skills. The ability to work independently and manage competing priorities. Happy to work from the Crawley office 3-4 days per week. Highly desirable Knowledge or experience of the Crowsnest Mission System. Defence, aerospace or mission-critical systems experience. Experience in field service or customer support environments. Understanding of reliability, maintainability and supportability engineering principles. Experience with DRACAS, LSA, RM&T or obsolescence management activities. Security Clearance Requirement: UK Eyes Only: Due to the nature of the work that we do at Thales, many of our roles are subject to security restrictions. This role requires you to be a UK National and achieve Security Clearance (SC) without any caveats. It would be advantageous if currently held, however, if not currently held, it is a requirement that the successful applicant undergo, achieve, and maintain SC Clearance prior to commencing employment. If approved by the MOD, a dual national from a non-ITAR country may be considered. To be eligible for full SC, you generally need to have resided in the UK for the last 5 years. In some circumstances, a minimum of 3 years’ residence in the UK over the last 5 years may be accepted, with additional overseas checks. Please visit the UKSV website for further guidance: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/united-kingdom-security-vetting-clearance-levels/national-security-vetting-clearance-levels. At Thales, we ensure equal opportunities, pay and working conditions for all. The benefits we offer include private medical insurance, buying or selling annual leave, cycle to work schemes, employee discounts, paid volunteering day, stocks and shares, annual bonus and much more depending on the role. Discover more about our programmes, employee networks, wellbeing policies, and inclusive features here. If this role isn’t quite right for you, we encourage you to join our talent community where your details will be shared with our recruitment teams for other potential opportunities.
